p.title: Aarav's balcony plants
p.challenge: Aarav thinks sunlight makes plants grow taller. Put his investigation steps in order

nodes.text: Observe: balcony plants look taller
nodes.info: Something he noticed and wondered about.

nodes.text: Hypothesis: more sunlight makes plants grow taller
nodes.info: A possible answer that can be tested.

nodes.text: Experiment: two similar pots, one in sun, one in a dim corner
nodes.info: Same plant, same soil, same water. Only the light is different.

nodes.text: Record the heights in a table every few days
nodes.info: This record is the data.

nodes.text: Does the data support the hypothesis?
nodes.info: Compare the heights of the two plants.

nodes.text: Conclude and share the results
nodes.info: Others can repeat the test to check it.

nodes.text: Change the hypothesis and test again
nodes.info: That is not failure. It is learning!

p.title: Isha's fair test: sugar in warm and cold water
p.challenge: Play Isha's experiment. At the question, choose what makes the test fair

nodes.text: Does sugar dissolve faster in warm water?
nodes.info: Isha wants to find out.

nodes.text: Change ONE thing: water temperature
nodes.info: This is the independent variable.

nodes.text: Measure: time for the sugar to dissolve
nodes.info: This is the dependent variable.

nodes.text: Is everything else kept the same?
nodes.info: Same amount of water, same amount and type of sugar, same glass, same stirring.

nodes.text: Fair test! Compare the two times
nodes.info: Now any difference is caused by the temperature alone.

nodes.text: Not fair: keep the controlled variables the same
nodes.info: If the sugar or stirring also changes, we cannot tell what caused the result.

p.title: Which microbe is it?
p.challenge: Use this key like a scientist: answer each question to sort a microbe into its group

nodes.text: Multiplies only inside other living cells?
nodes.info: Viruses are even smaller than bacteria.

nodes.text: Virus (causes cold and flu)
nodes.info: It can multiply only inside living cells.

nodes.text: Green? Makes food from sunlight?
Alga, like Spirogyra
nodes.info: Algae have chlorophyll and make their own food.

nodes.text: Fuzzy threads or budding cells?
nodes.info: Think of bread mould and yeast.

nodes.text: Fungus, like yeast or bread mould
nodes.info: Bread mould grows as fuzzy threads on damp bread.

nodes.text: Moves and catches food, like Amoeba?
Protozoan, like Amoeba or Paramecium
nodes.info: A protozoan causes malaria.

nodes.text: Bacterium, like Lactobacillus
nodes.info: Lactobacillus turns milk into curd.

p.title: How dosa batter rises
p.challenge: Put the steps in order to see how microbes make dosa batter rise

panels.t: Rice and urad dal are soaked in water.
They are ground into a smooth batter.
The batter is left overnight in a warm place.
Yeast and bacteria in the batter ferment it.
They give out carbon dioxide gas, which makes bubbles.
The batter has risen and is ready for soft dosas.

p.title: How malaria spreads
p.challenge: Mosquitoes are vectors. Put the steps of how malaria spreads in order

panels.t: A female Anopheles mosquito bites a person who has malaria.
It sucks up blood with the malaria parasite (a protozoan).
The same mosquito later bites a healthy person.
The parasite enters the healthy person's blood.
That person falls ill with malaria.

p.title: Make Sana's home dengue-safe
p.challenge: Dengue is spreading. Walk through the home check and choose what to do

nodes.text: Check coolers, pots, tyres and flower vases
nodes.info: Aedes mosquitoes lay eggs in still water.

nodes.text: Is water standing in any of them?
Empty, scrub and dry them
nodes.info: No still water means no place for mosquitoes to breed.

nodes.text: Use nets, repellent and full sleeves
nodes.info: This stops mosquitoes from biting.

nodes.text: Fewer mosquitoes, less dengue
nodes.info: Repeat the check every week.

p.title: Sea breeze or land breeze?
p.challenge: Choose day or night and follow the air to see which way the breeze blows

nodes.text: Land and sea at the coast
nodes.info: Land heats up and cools down faster than water.

nodes.text: Is it daytime?
Land is warmer than the sea
nodes.info: Warm air over the land expands, becomes lighter and rises: low pressure.

nodes.text: Sea breeze: cool air blows from sea to land
nodes.info: Air moves from high pressure to low pressure.

nodes.text: Land is cooler than the sea
nodes.info: Warm air over the sea rises: low pressure over the sea.

nodes.text: Land breeze: air blows from land to sea
nodes.info: Air moves from high pressure to low pressure.

p.title: Life of a cyclone
p.challenge: Put the story of a cyclone in order, from warm sea to safe shelter

panels.t: Warm ocean water heats the moist air above it.
The moist air rises, leaving a region of very low pressure.
Winds spiral in at high speed around a calm centre, the eye.
IMD tracks it with satellites and radar and issues warnings.
People move to cyclone shelters and fishermen stay off the sea.
